title: CAPTCHA and bot protection

requirements.text: CAPTCHA tokens (Turnstile, hCaptcha, reCAPTCHA) are verified server-side against the provider siteverify endpoint
Verification checks hostname, action, challenge age and (reCAPTCHA v3) score
Provider outages and malformed replies are refused by default; failing open is explicit
A solved challenge is accepted once, including under concurrent replays
A no-third-party option (honeypot with minimum fill time, proof of work) protects forms without image puzzles
The provider secret never appears in responses, errors or logs
Every failed check gets the same response, so attackers cannot tell which check failed
Repeated attempts from one client or key are throttled with 429 and Retry-After

evidence.name: success posts form-encoded secret, response and remoteip to the documented endpoint
wrong hostname, stale and future timestamps, and error codes are refused
action mismatch for Turnstile and reCAPTCHA
reCAPTCHA v3 low score is refused at the threshold
network failure is fail-closed by default and passes only with failOpen
PoW: concurrent replays of one solution succeed exactly once
honeypot: a filled hidden field and a too-fast submission are bots
the secret never appears in thrown configuration errors
protect(): passes good submissions, hides the failing check

implementations.notes: Replay protection is tested for the proof-of-work challenge; provider tokens rely on the provider's single-use check

evidence.name: concurrent requests on the memory store never exceed the limit
rateLimitResponse builds a 429 with Retry-After and RateLimit headers

notes: Genlib does not generate image CAPTCHAs; it verifies provider CAPTCHAs and offers honeypot and proof-of-work.
